## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D tactical shooter inspired by CrossFire, designed for phones and tablets.

## Requirements
- Deliver a playable game without asking clarifying questions.
- Provide usable touch controls for phone and tablet play.

## Decisions
- Implemented a browser-based Three.js first-person shooter with keyboard/mouse and mobile touch controls.
- Chose an original “BLACKSITE PROTOCOL” setting and visual design.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the game interface, responsive layouts, Three.js arena, weapon, enemies, three waves, combat, movement, damage, pickups, minimap, audio, and game-state UI.
- Added Vite development/build/preview scripts; `npm run build` and `node --check src/main.js` succeeded.

### Active
- Test gameplay and mobile/desktop layouts in a browser; address runtime or interaction issues and capture/inspect a current JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- Browser screenshot attempt failed with `net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED` after the development server stopped; the server was restarted in the background, but browser testing remains pending.

## Next Move
1. Confirm the Vite server is available at `http://127.0.0.1:5173/`, then test the game in Chromium.
2. Exercise deploy, movement/aiming, firing, reload, pause, defeat/victory, retry, and touch controls; fix any issues.
3. Capture and inspect a current small JPEG screenshot, then rerun the production build.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Three.js setup and gameplay implementation.
- `src/style.css`: Game visuals and responsive/touch layouts.
- `index.html`: Menus, HUD, controls, and result screens.
- `package.json`: Vite scripts and dependencies.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked, including `dist/`.
- Dependencies include `three@0.187.0`, `vite@7.2.2`, and Fontsource Rajdhani/IBM Plex Mono.

## Objective
- Complete and verify a playable, phone- and tablet-friendly 3D tactical shooter inspired by CrossFire.

## Requirements
- Deliver a playable game without asking clarifying questions.
- Provide usable touch controls for phone and tablet play.

## Decisions
- Built a browser-based Three.js shooter with desktop and mobile controls and an original “BLACKSITE PROTOCOL” setting.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented the arena, enemies, three waves, combat, movement, pickups, minimap, audio, HUD, menus, and touch controls.
- Chromium smoke test confirmed WebGL, gameplay start, firing, pause/resume, and reload completion.
- Emulated a 390×844 mobile viewport: touch controls display and joystick/fire button fit within the screen.
- Identified pointer-lock promise rejections and added a helper that catches rejected requests.
- Added `favicon.svg` and linked it in `index.html` to address the missing favicon request.

### Active
- Verify touch control interactions, defeat/victory, retry, and responsive layouts on phone and tablet sizes.
- Recheck browser console and confirm the pointer-lock and favicon changes resolve the logged errors.

### Blocked
- Full defeat/victory, retry, and touch interaction tests remain incomplete.

## Next Move
1. Rerun Chromium tests after the latest changes; verify mobile touch input and responsive layouts.
2. Test defeat/victory and retry flows; investigate any remaining console errors.
3. Run `npm run build` and `node --check src/main.js`.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Three.js setup, gameplay, input handling, and latest pointer-lock handling.
- `src/style.css`: responsive layout and touch controls.
- `index.html`: menus, HUD, touch markup, and favicon link.
- `favicon.svg`: new favicon asset.
- `/tmp/opencode/cdp-test.mjs`: Chromium gameplay smoke test.
- `/tmp/opencode/cdp-diagnostics.mjs`: mobile viewport and console diagnostics.

## Important Context
- Project changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked, including `dist/`.
- Before the latest changes, the console showed `NotAllowedError: A user gesture is required to request Pointer Lock.` as “Uncaught (in promise)” and a 404; the pointer-lock request now catches rejection, and the favicon was added, but neither fix has been retested.
- Mobile controls were checked for visibility and positioning only, not functional input.
